Step 2: Refine the search to specifically target studies reporting the bandgap of 10.00% Ni-doped ZnO. Prioritize experimental and theoretical papers that directly address this specific doping concentration.

Step 3: Investigate the combined system by searching for literature on 'graphene Ni-doped ZnO bandgap', 'graphene/Ni-doped ZnO heterostructure bandgap', or 'graphene-ZnO composite with Ni doping bandgap'. This step aims to understand how graphene interacts with and modifies the electronic structure of the doped ZnO.

Step 4: Analyze the retrieved scientific literature from all previous steps. Identify and cross-reference studies that provide direct measurements or theoretical calculations of the bandgap for the complete material system (graphene, 10.00% Ni-doped ZnO). Pay attention to synthesis methods and measurement techniques.

Step 5: Extract the most relevant bandgap value(s) from the identified studies. If a precise match for the entire system is not found, synthesize information from the closest related studies to provide an estimated range or a qualitative description of the expected bandgap, noting any influencing factors or discrepancies.

Title: Opening of a Gap in Graphene Due to Supercell Potential: Group Theory Point of View. Abstract: We analyze in the framework of the space group theory the change of the dispersion law in grapenein the vicinity of the (former) Dirac points due to application of supercell potential with the $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ space periodicity and the same point symmetry as graphene.

raw_tool_data.text: Title: Symmetry classification of energy bands in graphene and silicene. Abstract: We present the results of the symmetry classification of the electron energy bands in graphene and silicene using group theory algebra and the tight--binding approximation. The analysis is performed both in the absence and in the presence of the spin-orbit coupling. We also discuss the bands merging in the Brillouin zone symmetry points and the conditions for the latter to become Dirac points.

Abstract: In this chapter, semi-analytical models for the calculation of the quantum capacitance of both monolayer and bilayer graphene and its nanoribbons, are presented. Since electron-hole puddles are experimental facts in all graphene samples, they have been incorporated in our calculations.
